title: Choose a source-backed check for a native APEX prototype
changes: Find supported checks in the selected Forms source and show the exact source file, module, block and button.
Include one check in a new conversion only after explicit partial-scope approval; retain the exact selection through saved progress and supported recovery.
Generate a separate native APEX check from a proven initial null-or-zero count predicate, without inventing the original approval action.
Require four source-bound synthetic test cases, exact browser outcomes and before/after row checks before releasing the new profile's export.
Keep lookup, stale-source, timeout and continue-without-check choices explicit in the business-user interface.
Preserve older runs and their original browser proof with a separate versioned check-profile runner.
Include the preceding download correction and bounded history-preservation fixes; deployment remains a separate checked step.
limitations: The new check recognizes one narrow, directly proven first count predicate. It is not a general PL/SQL translator or full button conversion.

The check reads saved synthetic detail rows. Empty grouping values and no matching rows pass; negative nonzero values are not rejected. Unsaved Forms buffers, later statements, exception handling and approval remain unconverted.
The source/API/UI and connectionless SQLcl checks do not prove installed fixture creation, actual Oracle browser behavior or a successful hosted download. Live acceptance remains pending.
The new omission route supports only the exact same-block redacted filter and ordering failure class before its reviewer starts. It does not recover hidden values or claim equivalent query behavior.

Historical review validation retains its byte-pinned implementation. Scoped reuse does not grant permission; wait allowances do not guarantee completion. Unknown outcomes require reconciliation, not automatic retry.
Server-side preparation requires operator configuration and testing. The hosted route accepts one FMB per request; MMB, OLB and PLL require the separate supported preparation route.
The focused prototype profile, current authority endpoint and private browser worker require explicit operator configuration and live checks.

The retained real-file run has completed OPAF review, APEX import, authenticated runtime checks and server-side SQL export on the lab target. UI download and exact-downloaded-byte fresh-ID import remain pending until the patch is deployed and exercised.
Any changed candidate requires its own independent review; a saved review is reusable only for the exact reconstructed candidate it approved.

Inert startup preservation grants no retry, execution, closure or acceptance. Mixed stages require a proven runtime candidate and one runtime target; not every unresolved boundary is supported. Actual host compatibility and coherent deployment remain separate gates.
Technical identifiers are retained; redaction receipts are not complete PII certification or processing permission.
APEX generated, technical checks passed and business acceptance remain separate. A prototype export does not prove clean-schema reimport, customer-target compatibility or business equivalence.
